en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Fifth Chapter
The Discussion on Knowledge of the Present.
Is there knowledge regarding the present? Yes.
“Does that knowledge know that knowledge by means of that knowledge?
“One should not say so.
…pe… “Does that knowledge know that knowledge by means of that knowledge?”
“Yes,” [you reply].
“Does that knowledge know that very knowledge as ‘knowledge’?
One should not say so … [and so on] …
By means of that knowledge, one knows that knowledge as "knowledge"?
Yes. Is that knowledge the object of that knowledge?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is that knowledge the object of that knowledge? Yes.
By that contact he touches that contact; by that feeling he feels that feeling;
by that perception he perceives that perception; by that volition he intends that volition; by that consciousness he cognizes that consciousness;
by that applied thought he applies thought to that applied thought; by that sustained thought he sustains thought on that sustained thought; by that rapture...
He cherishes that rapture; through that mindfulness he remembers that mindfulness; through that wisdom he understands that wisdom;
with that sword he cuts that sword; with that axe he hews that axe; with that adze he hews that adze;
with that adze he hews that adze; with that awl he sews that awl.
With that fingertip he touches that fingertip; with that tip of the nose he touches that tip of the nose;
with that head he touches that head; with that excrement he washes that excrement;
with that urine he washes that urine; with that saliva he washes that saliva; with that pus he washes that pus.
“Does that blood wash away this blood?
One should not say so… [and so on]… It should not be said—
“Is there knowledge regarding the present?”— Yes.
But when all conditioned phenomena are seen as impermanent, is that knowledge itself not also seen as impermanent?
“Yes.
“If, when all conditioned phenomena are seen as impermanent, that knowledge itself is also seen as impermanent, then indeed, sir, you must admit:
‘Knowledge exists in the present.’”
The Discussion on Knowledge of the Present is finished.
